subject: Recap: MAP technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks & ownership
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@healthgrid.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: MAP technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks & ownership

Thanks again for a productive call today — appreciate you walking through the integration surface and high-level goals. As promised, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) worksheet with a proposed technical-evaluation milestone. High-level summary below and specific asks for the next week.

Summary of proposed technical milestone:
- Objective: Validate model slate and performance envelope to hit product SLOs for HealthGrid clinical summarization.
- Success criteria (pass/fail gating):
  - P0: 95% of clinical notes must keep hallucination rate <= 2% per our eval prompts (see sheet 'Hallucination-sets').
  - P1: Average 99th-percentile latency (inference, end-to-end from request to streaming first-token) <= 420ms at 8 concurrent streams per GPU in your environment or equivalent baseline.
  - P2: Per-token cost target <= $0.0025 (tokenization & model execution at Redwood hosted baseline); we'll report normalized cost for on-premdedicated numbers.
- Model shortlist: LlamaX-13B-q4f, Falcon-40B-instruct, Mistral-Instruct-7B-quant. We recommend starting with the quantized 13B variant and one 40B to check quality/cost tradeoffs.

Key owners & asks (this week):
1) HealthGrid (Tom/Priya): share a ~5k-note representative sample (anonymized) and the top 20 prompt templates you use for summarization. Please upload to the Drive link or confirm we can pull from S3. (Due: 2027-05-25)
2) Redwood (Marissa): finalize benchmark harness and test data mapping; validate eval prompts from the sheet. (Due: 2027-05-27)
3) Redwood (Connor): spin up the initial bench harness with the three shortlisted models, run warmup runs, and share a first-pass latency/cost matrix. (Due: 2027-06-03)
4) Joint: 1-week rolling sync to review early failures and decide whether to add a second 40B candidate. (First sync: 2027-06-07)

Dependencies/risks:
- Need anonymized sample by 5/25 to keep timeline.
- If HealthGrid requires on-prem data handling for PII, bench environment will shift and may add setup time (~3 business days).

Next steps I will take now: attach MAP draft (v1), create HubSpot action items, and schedule the first bench sync for 6/7. If any of the success criteria above look off, call it out and we will adjust.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_draft_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), latency_benchmark-template.pdf (doc)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@healthgrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@healthgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: MAP technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks & ownership

Thanks Ben — this is a helpful starting point. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 
1) Latency: the 420ms number is for first-token streaming in our production infra (k8s w/ GPU nodes). We need to be explicit whether Redwood runs are measured on hosted or in our k8s cluster. Can Redwood provide a normalized baseline (e.g., reference hardware + SLO) so we can map reliably?
2) Model shortlist: can you add any safety/regression notes for the 40B candidate? We have strict safety/regulatory constraints and would like to understand risk delta between 13B quant and 40B.

We will upload a de-identified 1k-note sample today to the Drive (folder noted) and confirm whether we need an NDA for full sample sharing. Also — we need the evaluation to feed into procurement by mid-June; is the 6/7 sync aggressive for you?

— Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Product, Clinical AI | HealthGrid
priya.shah@healthgrid.com

To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@healthgrid.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@healthgrid.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: MAP technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks & ownership

+1 on clarifying baseline. Ben, I suggest we add a 'Reference baseline' tab in the MAP that shows: hardware (A100 80GB vs T4), batch size, sequence length assumptions (avg 512 tokens), and how we measure 99th-percentile end-to-end latency. That will make HealthGrid's mapping much simpler.

Technical suggestions for pass/fail thresholds (proposed by product):
- Hallucination (P0): <= 2% on the standardized hallucination probe for the 1k sample.
- Quality (P0.1): ROUGE-L and an expert adjudication sample where we require >= 0.82 normalized score on the 100-note adjudication set.
- Latency (P1): 99th <= 420ms at 8 concurrent streams on A100 baseline; if HealthGrid's infra is T4-class, we'll add an equivalent multiplier column.
- Cost (P2): show normalized cost per 1k notes at 75% token reduction assumptions.

Connor — can you confirm you have the bench harness forked and that the latency template PDF has the right measurement commands? I can take the lead on stitching the adjudication set and running the ROUGE calculations if you hand off the pipeline outputs.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions & Benchmarks | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: latency_benchmark-template.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@healthgrid.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@healthgrid.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: MAP technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks & ownership

Quick status: I forked the bench harness yesterday and wired the latency template. I will run the three-model sweep (LlamaX-13B-q4f, Falcon-40B-instruct, Mistral-7B-quant) against the 1k sample once HealthGrid uploads it to the Drive. Expected first-pass latency/cost matrix by 2027-06-03 as listed.

Notes on measurement:
- Using seq len 512 default but will also run 256 and 1024 samples to show sensitivity.
- For the 99th P99, I'll surface both raw ms and normalized ms based on A100 baseline per Marissa's tab.
- If HealthGrid asks for on-prem (non-hosted) runs, we will need their kubeconfig/endpoint access model or a shared VPN; that could add 3 business days.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

Attachment: healthgrid_sample_payloads.json (waiting for upload)

From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@healthgrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 May 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: MAP technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks & ownership

Thanks all — confirming we will upload a de-identified 1k sample by end of day today (folder: Drive/HealthGrid/Redwood/bench). We prefer Redwood to run initial hosted benchmarks against the A100 baseline and then advise on equivalent mappings for our infra (T4).

A few constraints from procurement/regulatory: we cannot provide kubeconfigs or VPN access without a completed DPA and a signed SCA. I will work with procurement to accelerate those docs, but please plan for the 3-business-day on-prem setup as a contingency.

Timeline note: procurement needs the bench report and suggested model recommendation by 2027-06-11 to make the next budget cycle. If we can keep the 6/7 sync and have the 6/3 first-pass numbers, that should be fine.

Tom Hsu
VP Product Strategy | HealthGrid
thsu@healthgrid.com
